Every meal is sized to your daily target of %1$s kcal: breakfast 25%%, lunch 35%%, snack 10%%, dinner 30%%.
Dishes from %1$s come first, plus everyday staples you can find anywhere.
Low budget: mostly affordable staples like lentils, eggs, rice and seasonal vegetables.
Medium budget: staples plus some chicken, fish and dairy.
Flexible budget: the widest variety, including premium fish and meat.
Diabetes: no added-sugar or high-glycemic dishes, and carbs stay around 60 g per meal so blood sugar stays steady.
IBS: low-FODMAP choices – no onion- or garlic-heavy, bean-heavy or spicy dishes.
Lactose intolerance: no milk-heavy dishes. Yogurt and cheese in small amounts are usually well tolerated.
Don\'t fancy a dish? Swap it – alternatives keep the same calories and respect your health needs.
Tap ⓘ on any dish to see what\'s in it and why it was chosen.
Plans are algorithm-generated and not medical advice. If you have a health condition, check your diet with your doctor or dietitian.

Gentle on blood sugar: low-to-medium glycemic carbs, no added sugar
Gentle on your gut: low-FODMAP, no onion- or garlic-heavy, bean-heavy or spicy ingredients
A familiar dish where you live – easy to find and cook
Plant protein from beans, lentils or soy
Filling for few calories – helps you stay in your deficit
Energy-dense and wholesome – supports your weight-gain goal
Oily fish: omega-3 fats for heart health
Portions are adjusted so every option keeps about the same calories.
Vitamins and fiber for few calories
A fresh day – start with breakfast.
🎉 You completed today\'s plan. Consistency is what changes results!
Tap a meal to see what\'s in it, or swap it if it doesn\'t suit you today.
Fill half your plate with vegetables first – it naturally keeps portions in check.
Drink a glass of water before each meal; thirst is often mistaken for hunger.
Cook a pot of lentils or rice once and use it in two meals – less time, less waste.
Eat slowly: it takes about 20 minutes for your body to feel full.
Protein and fiber keep you full longest – they are why your plan favours lentils, eggs and vegetables.
A 20-minute walk after dinner burns energy and helps digestion.
Add a handful of nuts or a spoon of peanut butter to snacks for easy, healthy calories.
Weigh in once a week at the same time – small trends matter more than daily changes.
Seasonal and local produce is cheapest and freshest – swap vegetables freely for what\'s in season.
Eat vegetables and protein before the rice or bread – it softens the blood-sugar rise.
Keep carbs similar at each meal and log your sugar to see how meals affect you.
Garlic- or onion-infused oil gives the flavour without the FODMAPs – remove the pieces before eating.
Log symptoms daily for two weeks – patterns show which foods suit you best.
Yogurt and hard cheese are usually tolerated better than milk, especially with a meal.
